item.title: China Takes Down Shanghai Party Boss Once Seen as Potential Leader
item.description: Chen Jining, the party secretary of Shanghai, has been placed under investigation on suspicion of severe violations of party discipline and state laws.

item.title: The Gap Between China’s Military Spectacle and Battlefield Reality
item.description: Plus, U.S. chip restrictions deepen China’s AI computing crunch and the shadow network behind Nvidia’s China chip-smuggling scandal resurfaces.

item.title: China to Suspend Some Critical-Material Export Curbs to U.S. Until January
item.description: China extended its suspension of export restrictions on some critical materials to the U.S., just days after last week’s Shenzhen summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

item.title: China’s Huawei Convicted of Fraud in U.S. Criminal Trial
item.description: A federal jury convicted the tech and telecom giant of fraud and other offenses but acquitted it of racketeering conspiracy.

item.description: The AI spy affair has spurred once-sidelined politicians to get tough on China.

item.title: China’s Push for Influence in the South Pacific Is Running Into Resistance
item.description: Washington is enjoying a boost in the region’s strategic islands as political winds shift and Australia pursues aggressive diplomacy.

item.title: As China Encroaches, Even New Zealand Is Getting Serious About Its Military
